desc:
Given an array nums of pairwise distinct integers, find the smallest absolute difference between any two of its elements. Return all pairs [a, b] of elements with a < b and b - a equal to that smallest difference.

List the pairs in ascending order (by a; since values are distinct, every a occurs in at most one pair).

For example, [4, 2, 1, 3] gives [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]], and [10, 1, 5, 12] gives [[10, 12]].
hints: Comparing all pairs works for tiny inputs but is O(n<sup>2</sup>) overall.
Which two elements can be at the minimum distance? Think about where such a pair sits once the numbers are in order.
Sort the array. The closest pairs are always neighbours in sorted order, so scan adjacent differences twice: once for the minimum, once to collect the pairs.
editorial: If two elements x < y had another element z strictly between them, then (x, z) would be closer than (x, y). So a minimum-difference pair is always adjacent in the sorted array. Sort, compute the minimum of s[i+1] - s[i], and then output every adjacent pair whose difference equals it.
Sorting costs O(n log n) and the two scans cost O(n). The output is already in ascending order because it is produced from the sorted array.
solution:
def minDiffPairs(nums):
    s = sorted(nums)
    best = min(s[i + 1] - s[i] for i in range(len(s) - 1))
    return [[s[i], s[i + 1]] for i in range(len(s) - 1) if s[i + 1] - s[i] == best]
